results:
The patent you're looking for appears to be **U.S. Patent 3,600,186**, "Low calorie fat-containing food compositions," assigned to Procter & Gamble and issued to Mattson et al. Note that the 1968 date is the filing date, not the issue date.

- **Filing and issue dates:** Google Patents lists the filing as April 23, 1968, with issue on August 17, 1971. US3600186A (en) * 1968-04-23 1971-08-17 Procter & Gamble Low calorie fat-containing food compositions
- **Subject matter:** A later P&G patent describes it as disclosing low calorie food compositions, including mayonnaise and salad dressing products, wherein at least a portion of the fat is replaced with certain nonabsorbable, nondigestible polyol polyesters.
- **Olestra connection:** Wikipedia says Volpenhein in 1968 while researching fats that could be more easily digested by premature infants. The olestra work came out of this research, though the sources I found don't explicitly tie the 1968 research to the 3,600,186 patent itself.

Other sources also cite it by number, including a 1987 European patent application, which refers to it as "U.S. Patent 3,600,186 to Mattson et al, issued August 17, 1971."

content.text:
**美国专利 US 3,600,186**,题为"Low calorie fat-containing food compositions"(低热量含脂肪食品组合物),受让人是宝洁(Procter & Gamble),发明人是 Mattson 等人。

- 1968 年 4 月 23 日申请,1971 年 8 月 17 日授权。
- 这个编号不是靠单独一份文件确认的。搜索结果中,Google Patents 的列表给出了申请和授权日期,一份 1987 年的欧洲专利申请也写了"U.S. Patent 3,600,186 to Mattson et al, issued August 17, 1971"。
- 搜索结果没有明确写出发明人除 Mattson 外还有 Volpenhein。他和这项专利的联系,我是根据他在 1968 年参与的相关研究(后来发展出 olestra)推断的。

Sources:
- [Olestra – Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olestra)
- [US5006360A – Low calorie fat substitute compositions resistant to laxative side effect – Google Patents](https://patents.google.com/patent/US5006360)
- [Low calorie fat materials that eliminate laxative side effect – Justia Patents](https://patents.justia.com/patent/6821545)
- [EP0375239B1 – EPO publication server](https://data.epo.org/publication-server/rest/v1.2/patents/EP0375239NWB1/document.xml)
